runs.request: I want to analyse particulate matter (PM2.5 and PM10) by country and year

question.instructions: Can the data catalogue answer this request as written?

criteria.answer: It names at least one pollutant, or asks for pollution, emissions or data in general, and at least one breakdown the catalogue holds: region, country or continent; month or year from 2015 to 2025; subsector or macrosector. A named place, period or sector counts as a breakdown.
criteria.clarify: It is about air pollution data but names no pollutant and no general term such as pollution or emissions, or it gives no breakdown at all.
criteria.reject: It is off-topic, or it needs something the catalogue does not hold: cities, streets, stations, days, hours, weeks, years outside 2015 to 2025, forecasts, pollutants such as ozone, or other kinds of pollution such as water or noise.

notes: Global Facility Emissions Inventory is summed over sector but covers only 12 of 13 subsectors
European Air Emissions Reporting is summed over sector but covers only 9 of 13 subsectors
solutions.summary: Sources: Global Facility Emissions Inventory (research, updated 2025); National Emissions Compendium (official, updated 2024); European Air Emissions Reporting (official, updated 2025). 3 countries: Italy, Spain, Poland. Years: 2021 to 2023 (3 covered). Pollutants: CO2, CO2e (100-year), CO2e (20-year), CH4, N2O, PM2.5, PM10, NOx and 16 more. Global Facility Emissions Inventory is summed over sector but covers only 12 of 13 subsectors. European Air Emissions Reporting is summed over sector but covers only 9 of 13 subsectors.

legend.0: It does not match the preference.

explanation.text:
1 solution hold CO2, CO2e (100-year), CO2e (20-year), CH4, N2O, PM2.5 and 18 more by country and year.
First: A, Global Facility Emissions Inventory + National Emissions Compendium + European Air Emissions Reporting, covering 3 countries, 2021 to 2023. Preference fit 2.0 of 3 (100% confident in its most likely level). Caution: Global Facility Emissions Inventory is summed over sector but covers only 12 of 13 subsectors; European Air Emissions Reporting is summed over sector but covers only 9 of 13 subsectors.
